query: What are the common advantage attributes of airlines whose overall rating is high?

per_column.name: seat_comfort_and_spaciousness
per_column.rationale: Physical comfort of the seating is a genuine constitutive aspect of an airline's product/service quality, hence a facet of its competitive advantage.

per_column.name: aircraft_modernity_and_condition
per_column.rationale: The state and modernity of the fleet is an aspect of the airline's product offering and thus a part of its competitive advantage.

per_column.name: ground_service_efficiency
per_column.rationale: Ground handling/check-in efficiency is a distinct dimension of the airline's service experience, a constitutive facet.

per_column.name: value_for_money_perception
per_column.rationale: Value-for-money is an aggregate summary judgment of the whole offering (price vs. total quality), not a distinct constitutive part; it restates the overall advantage rather than decomposing it, and overlaps with all other facets.

per_column.name: food_and_beverage_quality
per_column.rationale: Catering quality is a discrete aspect of the inflight product and a legitimate facet of competitive advantage.

judge.rationale: Four of the five columns are true constitutive facets (seat comfort, aircraft condition, ground service, catering), carving relatively distinct aspects of the airline product. Mutual exclusivity is lowered because value_for_money_perception is an aggregate summary of the whole offering that overlaps with every other facet rather than being an independent aspect. Exhaustiveness is moderate: important constitutive facets are missing, notably inflight staff/cabin service, inflight entertainment, punctuality/reliability, and network/schedule/route breadth, so the set does not fully cover the concept's main aspects.
